title: Certificates of Deposit: When a Grace Top-Up Is Written and for What Sum
content:
This page brings together, for Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit, the single decision on a grace top-up aimed at the Jumbo Bonus: whether one is written, and at what sum.

## Rule

A top-up is written, at the top-up sum sized from the gap below the Jumbo Bonus threshold, only when every one of these is true at once:

- the certificate is open to grace actions, will renew into its own tier, and its tier offers the Jumbo Bonus and accepts grace add-ons;
- its interest disposition names no closed payout account;
- its ledger-built principal is below the Jumbo Bonus threshold;
- the top-up sits inside both what the grace period can still take and what the owner's savings can supply.

In every other case the sum written is nothing. A top-up that does not fit is never trimmed to fit; the answer is then no top-up.

## Truth table (hypothetical; top-up sized at USD 3779.55)

| Open to grace, same-tier renewal, tier features | Interest disposition names no closed account | Principal below threshold | Top-up within room and savings | Written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | USD 3779.55 |
| Yes | No | Yes | Yes | nothing |
| Yes | Yes | No | (not relevant) | nothing |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | No | nothing |
| No | Yes | Yes | Yes | nothing |
